All You Need To Know

[h1]Introduction:[h1]
Hello my name is Lock, my review will be available in two formats: a short summery which will be a short review and an in-depth review. This review is being written from the perspective of someone who has not played the previous installments of the ARMA franchise. 

[h1]Short Summery:[/h1] 
ARMA 3 is a near future military simulator from developer Bohemia Interactive. Players who are looking for the most entertainment will find it in multiplayer as single-player while visually stunning is ultimately forgettable. The multiplayer provides a wide variety of community created and supported content but as a result each server will provide different experiences in terms of computer performance community interaction, and overall experience. The game is graphically demanding and poorly optimized as a result a moderately high end CPU and modern graphics card is highly recommended. The game features solid replay value for multiplayer enthusiast but little for people looking for a single player experience. Ultimately if you’re looking for a brand new multiplayer experience unlike one you have ever experienced before I highly suggest playing ARMA 3. 

[h1] In-Depth Review:[h1]

[b]Single-player[/b] 
I personally haven’t spent a lot of time in ARMA 3’s single-player as I believe it is dwarfed by the multiplayer experience. If you’re looking for a game that has an extensive military campaign and have no intentions of playing the multiplayer then I am not sure if this game will be worth your money. The campaign experience for me thus far has been ultimately forgettable despite a visually stunning presentation. 

[b]Multiplayer[/b]
While the single-player is forgettable the multiplayer is [i]unforgettable[/i] giving the player a unique military simulator experience that no other game on the market can deliver. Depending on what game mode you’re playing you could find yourself in a large scale combat simulation battling the AI to take towns, power stations, and other objectives with 39-59 other players or find yourself in an extensively designed RPG, survival game, or large scale free for all. Speaking of game modes it should be mentioned that the games multiplayer is completely supported by the community. Nearly all (if not all) of the servers you find on multiplayer are created and supported by the community. This is both fantastic and sometimes annoying as some servers are scripted and maintained better than others. 
In-terms of mechanics ARMA 3’s controls are daunting to someone who is new to the franchise. The keyboard commands are extensive and require a bit of patients, trial and error, asking the community, and reading the field manual. Despite the controls being daunting they provide the player with an unprecedented ability to control himself and the environment. 
If you’re a player who doesn’t necessarily like foot solider combat ARMA provides a library of military vehicles from tanks to transport helicopters. Again the controls here are complicated and I highly suggest going into editor and quickly creating a scenario before attempting to fly something on a live server. Again though, once you have mastered the controls it opens up a wealth of control that other games do not allow. 
Finally the multiplayer community differs depending on what server you’re on; however, my experience has been fantastic. The community is fun, helpful, and varies so much that any player should be able to find the experience they’re looking for on ARMA 3. 
Tip: If you’re looking for a large scale combat scenario my personal favorite coming from games like Battlefield and Call of Duty is “Invade and Annex” a popular game mode on ARMA 3 where 60 players conduct military operations against the AI to take objectives.

[b]Performance[/b] 
ARMA 3 is a graphically intensive game especially in multiplayer as a result the game is one of the most demanding on a computer. In addition to being demanding the game also isn’t the best optimized in terms of performance this is partially due to the developer and the community created content. Players who are looking for a solid experience should have computers equipped to handle the task with moderately high end CPUs and modern graphics cards. 

[b]Replay Value[/b] 
As previously stated the single-player experience doesn’t offer much replay value; however, the multiplayer is packed with game modes that will provide players with hundreds if not thousands of hours of entertainment.
